skill.name: asd-ste100
skill.description: Rewrite ambiguous technical English using ASD-STE100-inspired rules. Preserve facts, conditions, and uncertainty while checking selected structural patterns with a local Python linter.
skill.summary: Clarify technical English with controlled-language rewrites and local structural linting.
skill.author: danyuchn

security_audit.summary: All 235 static findings are false positives involving Markdown syntax, parser fixtures, reference URLs, documented installation, and isolated self-test files. The linter reads supplied text locally and writes only temporary self-test fixtures. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, exfiltration, hidden execution, or malicious obfuscation in the reviewed files.

content.user_title: Clarify Technical English With ASD-STE100 Rules
content.value_statement: Ambiguous technical English can cause readers and agents to misinterpret instructions. This skill applies controlled-language rewrite guidance and local structural checks to make wording clearer.
actual_capabilities: Rewrite tool descriptions, error messages, and agent instructions using short sentences and explicit conditions.
Apply Strict mode to instructions and STE-flavored mode to explanatory prose.
Provide rewritten text by default or a before-and-after rule table on request.
Check semicolons, sentence length, selected phrasal verbs, nominalizations, marketing adjectives, synonym rotation, and supported list endings.
Report possible passive voice and compound tenses as advisory findings without automatically rejecting modal uncertainty.
Lint standard input or local files with JSON output, configurable violation baselines, and rule disabling.
limitations: The official approved-word dictionary is not included, so exact vocabulary compliance and certified ASD-STE100 compliance are not guaranteed.
The linter uses heuristics, misses some grammar and Markdown cases, and does not check noun-cluster length.
Structural linting does not compare original and rewritten text or prove that facts, conditions, and requirement strength remain unchanged.
The skill targets English technical prose, not creative or persuasive copy; the bundled linter requires Python 3.

use_cases.title: Clarify Agent Tool Contracts
use_cases.description: Rewrite tool descriptions with explicit actions, conditions, and fallback behavior while preserving uncertainty.

use_cases.title: Review Operational Instructions
use_cases.description: Simplify procedures and error messages, then inspect structural lint findings before publishing.

use_cases.description: Use STE-flavored mode to reduce dense wording and inconsistent terminology in explanatory documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify One Instruction
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this instruction in Strict mode: [text]. Return only the rewrite. Preserve every fact, condition, and uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify a short technical instruction.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Documentation Rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this paragraph in STE-flavored mode: [text]. Show the before-and-after rule table. Note any wording you retain to preserve precision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review changes to explanatory prose.

prompt_templates.prompt: Run the bundled structural linter on [file] with JSON output and baseline [N]. Summarize hard and advisory findings. Do not modify the file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess structural violations in existing documentation.

prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite [text] in Strict mode for a downstream agent. Preserve conditions, exceptions, numbers, and uncertainty. Show the rule table. Identify unresolved ambiguities without inventing facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review instructions where incorrect interpretation has operational consequences.

best_practices: Select the rewrite mode based on whether the text describes a procedure or explains a concept.
Compare the rewrite with the source for facts, conditions, exceptions, numbers, and uncertainty.
Review lint findings individually and consult the official dictionary when approved vocabulary is required.
anti_patterns: Treating a clean lint result as proof of semantic fidelity or certified STE compliance.
Removing uncertainty, safety conditions, or exceptions merely to meet a sentence-length target.
Applying strict controlled-language rules to creative or persuasive text that depends on voice and nuance.

faq.question: Does this skill certify ASD-STE100 compliance?
faq.answer: No. It provides STE-inspired guidance and structural checks, not certification or complete validation against the official dictionary.

faq.question: What is the difference between the two modes?
faq.answer: Strict mode applies the full rewrite guidance to technical instructions. STE-flavored mode retains structural discipline but treats lexical restrictions as advisory.

faq.question: What does the Python linter require?
faq.answer: It requires Python 3 and uses only the standard library. It accepts standard input or local file paths.

faq.question: Does linting send my documents to a remote service?
faq.answer: The bundled linter processes text locally and contains no network requests. The recommended third-party installer separately documents install telemetry and an opt-out.

faq.question: Does a clean lint result prove that a rewrite preserves meaning?
faq.answer: No. The linter checks selected structural patterns. Review the source and rewrite to verify facts, conditions, uncertainty, and requirement strength.

faq.question: Can I request an explanation instead of only the rewrite?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask to show the diff or explain the changes. The skill then provides a before-and-after table naming the relevant rules.
